title: Marked universality (U3 v001)
statement: For every sequence $s$ over $\mathbb N_{>0}$, $D(\iota(s))=s$ for the marked history $\iota(s)$.
hypotheses: Routing $P(a,b)$ = lex-first shortest path; $P(a,a)=(a,4a,a)$; marks at observation positions.
falsification_gate: decode failure on any marked history

title: Exact segmentation ambiguity (U3-COR)
statement: For every $L\ge1$ some lex-first geodesic of length $L$ has exactly $M=2^{L-1}$ compatible mark assignments; always $M\le 2^{L-1}$.
hypotheses: Connected, infinite, locally finite graph; subpath lemma.
falsification_gate: a geodesic whose $M\ne 2^{L-1}$ with all internal marks valid

title: Suspension facts (U3 v001)
statement: Golden-mean towers: period 2 for 56 embeddings in $\{1..8\}$; renewal equation $1-w-w^{d}=0$, $w=\lambda^{-2}$; Abramov relation; 3-symbol period depends on embedding (53 period 2, 31 period 1 among 84 triples).
falsification_gate: any listed embedding with a different period

title: Intrinsic admissibility facts (U3 v001)
statement: $X_r(F)$ is a 1-step SFT with reflexive symmetric pair relation; $G$ is triangle-free; a 4-cycle ($2,8,36,9$) and a 5-cycle ($6,24,96,784,27$) exist, so $\mathrm{girth}=4$, odd girth $=5$.
falsification_gate: a triangle in $G$; a pair relation that is not symmetric

title: SELECT-II digraph facts (S2.1--S2.3, S2.5, S2.10, S2.12)
statement: Arrows $m\to m(N+1)^2/N$ for $N\mid m$; outdegree $\tau(m)$, indegree $R(t)=\#\{d\ge2:d^2\mid t\}$; every arrow multiplies by $\ge4$ (acyclic); edge label identifiable; occurrence = edge; $\sum_{t\le5000}R=3124$, $\sum H=8283$.
hypotheses: Frozen SELECT-II v001/v002 records (registry ids S2.1, S2.2, S2.3, S2.5, S2.10, S2.12).
falsification_gate: a mismatch between the engine of this package and the frozen records

title: Faithful marked-history representation
statement: Alphabet $A$ (countable), injection $e:A\to\mathbb N_{>0}$, routing convention $P$, observation marks; \emph{faithful} means a decoder recovers $s$ from $(\iota_e(s),\text{marks})$.
falsification_gate: n/a

title: Largest representable class
statement: Marked-history representation exists for sequences (finite, one- or two-sided infinite) over $A$ iff $|A|\le\aleph_0$. No faithful representation exists over an uncountable alphabet.
hypotheses: $e$ injective; sequences of letters, not of real-valued data.
falsification_gate: an injection from an uncountable set into $\mathbb N$
proof_note: Sufficiency is U3.1a; necessity: $e$ injective into a countable set.

title: Computability transfer
statement: If $e$ is computable then $s\mapsto\iota_e(s)$ is computable (stream-wise) and $\iota_e(s)\mapsto s$ is computable given the marks; hence $s$ is computable iff its marked history is. The neighbour map is computable (factorisation); feasibility beyond the certification bound ($3.3\times10^{24}$) is a separate, experimental level.
hypotheses: Exact integer arithmetic; certification policy RN-0.
falsification_gate: a computable $s$ with non-computable $\iota_e(s)$ for computable $e$
proof_note: BFS balls are finite (local finiteness), so $d_G$ and $P$ are computable.

title: Segmentation information is exact and tight
statement: Unmarked walks need $\lceil\log_2M(w)\rceil\le L-1$ extra bits to decode, and $L-1$ bits are necessary for some walks of every length.
falsification_gate: see F.U3.1b

title: Bounded route cost for finite alphabets
statement: For every $k\ge3$ there is an embedding of a $k$-letter alphabet with all pairwise distances $\le2$ (a vertex $x$ with $\deg x\ge k-1$ and $k-1$ of its neighbours), so every transition costs at most $2$ steps (repeats cost $2$ by convention). Minimal such radius: $r^*(2)=1$, $r^*(k)=2$ for $k\ge3$.
falsification_gate: a $k$ for which no vertex of degree $\ge k-1$ exists, or three vertices pairwise adjacent
proof_note: $\tau(x)\to\infty$; closed neighbourhood of $x$ has diameter $\le2$; triangle-free excludes radius 1 for $k\ge3$.

title: No bounded cost for infinite alphabets
statement: If $A$ is infinite and $e$ injective then $\sup_{a,b}d_G(e(a),e(b))=\infty$; hence the full shift over an infinite alphabet has unbounded roof.
falsification_gate: an infinite subset of $V$ of bounded diameter
proof_note: Balls of finite radius are finite.

title: Eccentricity growth of the identity embedding
statement: Growth rate of $\max_{n\le N}d_G(1,n)$ is unknown; trivially $\le6(N-1)$ from bounded successor distance; no data or rate is claimed.
falsification_gate: a proof or counterexample of any specified rate

title: Discrete suspension (Kakutani tower)
statement: Base $(X,\sigma)$ a subshift over $A$ with embedding $e$; roof $r(s)=d_G(e(s_0),e(s_1))$ ($=2$ if $s_0=s_1$); tower $\{(s,j):0\le j<r(s)\}$ with the primitive successor map.
hypotheses: $r$ depends on two coordinates and is a positive integer; bounded when $A$ finite.
falsification_gate: n/a

title: Return-map conjugacy
statement: The first-return map of the tower to the base section $\{j=0\}$ is conjugate to $\sigma$.
falsification_gate: a sequence whose first return is not $\sigma(s)$

title: Measure entropy (Abramov)
statement: For ergodic $\mu$ with $\bar r=\int r\,d\mu<\infty$: $h_{\mu^r}=h_\mu/\bar r$.
status: Standard (Abramov); numerics in U3 agree to $10^{-16}$
falsification_gate: a Markov measure with $h_{\mu^r}\ne h_\mu/\bar r$

title: Topological entropy of the tower
statement: For an irreducible 1-step SFT base with transition matrix $B$ and two-coordinate roof, $h_{top}$ of the tower is $\log\lambda$ with $\lambda>1$ the largest solution of $\rho\big(B\circ[\lambda^{-r(a,b)}]\big)=1$ (pressure equation $P(-h\,r)=0$). Golden mean: $1-w-w^{d}=0$, $w=\lambda^{-2}$. In general $h_{top}\ge h_\mu/\bar r$ for every ergodic $\mu$; equality for the Parry measure is \emph{not} asserted beyond the golden-mean $(2,d,d)$ family, where it holds iff $d=2$.
hypotheses: Irreducible SFT base; the general `iff constant roof' claim is withdrawn (U3-COR).
falsification_gate: an embedding whose expanded-graph entropy differs from the root of the renewal equation

title: Parity-period theorem
statement: Let the base pair relation be symmetric and let an irreducible component $C$ contain a self-transition. Then the period of the tower over $C$ is $1$ or $2$, and equals $2$ iff there is $f:C\to\mathbb Z/2$ with $d_G(a,b)\equiv f(a)+f(b)\pmod 2$ on every allowed pair $a\ne b$. In particular the golden-mean tower has period $2$ for \emph{every} embedding.
hypotheses: Symmetric base relation; at least one loop (roof $2$) in $C$.
falsification_gate: a symmetric base component with a loop whose tower period is $>2$, or a golden-mean embedding of period $1$
proof_note: The loop gives closed sum $2$, so period divides $2$; all closed sums even iff a parity potential exists. Golden mean: $f(0)=0$, $f(1)=d\bmod2$.

title: Mixing criterion and embedding dependence
statement: If the base is an irreducible aperiodic SFT, the tower is topologically mixing iff its period is $1$. Mixing of the tower is therefore a property of $(\text{base},e)$, not of the base alone: for the 3-letter full shift, $\{1,2,3\}$ gives period $2$ while $\{1,2,5\}$ gives period $1$.
status: Standard criterion + exact certificates (closed sums $5+3+5=13$ odd)
falsification_gate: recomputed distances not equal to $5,3,5$ for $\{1,2,5\}$

title: Recurrence, ergodicity, periodic points
statement: A base periodic orbit with roof sum $R$ yields a tower periodic orbit of period $R$; the tower measure is ergodic iff the base measure is; Poincar\'e recurrence holds for finite tower measure ($\bar r<\infty$).
falsification_gate: a tower periodic point not arising from a base cycle

title: What the suspension does not preserve
statement: (i) entropy $h_{top}$ of the tower depends on $e$ (golden mean: $d=2$ vs $d=5$ give $0.2406$ vs $0.1406$), so towers over the same base can be non-conjugate; (ii) period and mixing depend on $e$ (T5); (iii) $h_{top}\neq h_{top}(\text{base})/\bar r$ in general.
falsification_gate: two embeddings with equal data but different entropy

title: Metric (graph-intrinsic) admissibility rules
statement: A rule of memory $m$ on a finite window $F\subset V$ is a predicate $\Phi$ on $(m{+}1)$-tuples that depends only on the matrix $(d_G(x_i,x_j))_{i,j\le m}$; $X_\Phi(F)$ = sequences all of whose $(m{+}1)$-blocks satisfy $\Phi$. $X_r(F)$ is $m=1$, $\Phi=[d\le r]$.
falsification_gate: n/a

title: Structure of $X_r(F)$
statement: $X_r(F)$ is a 1-step SFT whose pair relation is reflexive and symmetric; fixed points $=|F|$.
falsification_gate: a non-symmetric or non-reflexive pair relation

title: Fixed-point dichotomy
statement: For every metric rule $\Phi$ of any memory $m$ on a finite $F$: the number of fixed points of $X_\Phi(F)$ is $0$ or $|F|$. Hence a target SFT with $f\ge1$ fixed points is conjugate to a metric-rule shift only on exactly $f$ letters, all of them constants. The golden-mean shift ($f=1$, entropy $\log\varphi$) is conjugate to none.
falsification_gate: a metric rule with a constant accepted for some letters but not others
proof_note: Every constant window $(x,\dots,x)$ has the zero distance matrix, so its admissibility does not depend on $x$.

title: Real-spectrum obstruction (memory 1)
statement: A memory-1 metric shift has a symmetric transition matrix, hence real spectrum; the sequence $p_n=\operatorname{tr}B^n$ of periodic-point counts determines the nonzero spectrum, so an SFT with a non-real nonzero eigenvalue is not conjugate to any memory-1 metric shift. Example: the 3-cycle with loops, $B=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&1&0\\0&1&1\\1&0&1\end{psmallmatrix}$, spectrum $\{2,1+\omega,1+\bar\omega\}$.
hypotheses: Memory 1 only; memory $\ge2$ rules may be asymmetric --- OPEN.
falsification_gate: a symmetric matrix with the same $\operatorname{tr}B^n$ as $B$
proof_note: Newton identities recover the nonzero spectrum from $(\operatorname{tr}B^n)_n$.

title: Triangle-free entropy gap at radius 1
statement: For $k\ge3$ the full $k$-shift is not conjugate to any $X_1(F)$: conjugacy forces $|F|=k$ (T2), the pair graph is triangle-free (F.U3.3), and $\rho(A+I)=1+\rho(A)\le1+\sqrt{m}\le1+k/2<k$ (Nosal; Mantel). For radius 2 the full $k$-shift is realised by a star (U4.1-T4).
falsification_gate: a triangle-free graph on $k$ vertices with $\rho(A+I)\ge k$
proof_note: Classical inputs: Mantel (edge bound), Nosal (spectral bound) --- prior-art review pending.

title: Non-SFT systems are excluded
statement: Being an SFT is a conjugacy invariant; every $X_\Phi(F)$ is an SFT; hence no non-SFT subshift (e.g.\ the even shift, Sturmian shifts) is conjugate to a finite-memory metric shift. Rules with unbounded memory are outside the class.
falsification_gate: a finite-memory metric shift that is not an SFT

title: Finite-graph realisability
statement: Every finite graph is an induced subgraph of $G^{(r)}$ (vertices adjacent iff $d_G\le r$) for some $r$. If true, every reflexive symmetric memory-1 SFT with loops everywhere is $X_r(F)$ for some $r$.
hypotheses: Bounded evidence only: 30/30 connected graphs on $\le5$ vertices at $r=2,3$; $K_{2,3}$ not found at $r=1$ (U3 v001).
falsification_gate: a finite graph not embeddable at any $r$ (needs proof); a $\le6$-vertex graph failing at $r\le3$ within bounds

title: Rigidity and definability cost
statement: $\mathrm{Aut}(G)$ is trivial. If so, every vertex is definable from the graph (vertex $1$ is the unique vertex of degree $1$), and `naming' a vertex costs its description length --- the formal price of leaving the metric-rule class.
hypotheses: Local probe is inconclusive: degree-coloured balls of radius 2, 3 have a nontrivial automorphism group of order 2 (boundary symmetry only).
falsification_gate: a nontrivial automorphism of $G$

title: Explicit counterexamples to unrestricted intrinsic universality
statement: (a) golden mean (T2); (b) the 3-cycle with loops (T3); (c) full $k$-shift ($k\ge3$) at $r=1$ (T4); (d) any non-SFT (T5); (e) the \emph{directed} SELECT-II digraph represents no sequence with a descent (U4.5-S2d). Each is a theorem about the stated class, not about every conceivable intrinsic grammar.
falsification_gate: a missing hypothesis in any component

title: Three tiers and the knowledge ledger
statement: \emph{Representation}: a coding with decoder. \emph{Finite-control generation}: a program of $K$ declared bits that drives graph moves. \emph{Intrinsic generation}: no sequence-specific input; the orbit is determined by graph structure (and the start vertex). Ledger: $L(s)$ steps, $M(s)$ segmentation bits, $C_{route}$, $C_{cert}$, $K(e,P)$ reported separately.
falsification_gate: n/a

title: Counting bound
statement: A generator with $K$ declared bits produces at most $2^{K+1}-1$ distinct sequences; to cover all $2^n$ words over two letters one needs $K\ge n-1$. Only countably many sequences are produced by any fixed-program intrinsic dynamics (one orbit per start vertex).
falsification_gate: a generator with fewer than $n-1$ bits producing all $2^n$ words

title: Representation adds no sequence-independent information
statement: $K(\iota_e(s))=K(s)+O(1)$, with the constant depending only on the fixed program for $G$, $P$, $e$. A sequence-specific route table has at least the complexity of the sequence.
falsification_gate: a sequence whose marked history is simpler than the sequence by more than $O(1)$
proof_note: Invariance theorem for Kolmogorov complexity; two computable maps.

title: Recognition is intrinsic; scanning order is imported
statement: The predicate `$p$ prime $\iff\deg(p)=2$' is intrinsic to $G$. Listing the primes by scanning $\mathbb N$ with a bounded successor route and filtering by degree uses an imported enumeration of $V$ (finite control, $O(1)$ declared bits, certification cost $C_{cert}$ large); it is finite-control generation, not intrinsic generation.
hypotheses: Frozen TI-DYN degree--primality theorem and U1-BND bounded successor distance as recorded; not re-derived here.
falsification_gate: a prime of degree $\ne2$ or a non-prime of degree 2

title: Import obligation: RN negative results
statement: RN v001 classification of ranked-neighbour trajectories (stuck, divergent, prime visits) is imported with hashes in the U4 body; none of it is restated here.
falsification_gate: hash mismatch of the RN release

title: $G$ is the underlying graph of the SELECT-II digraph
statement: The edge set $\{kN,k(N+1)^2\}$ of $G$ equals the set of SELECT-II arrows $m\to m(N+1)^2/N$, $N\mid m$, forgetting orientation.
falsification_gate: a pair $(m,t)$ adjacent in one and not the other

title: Degree identity
statement: $\deg x=\tau(x)+R(x)$, $R(x)=\#\{d\ge2:d^2\mid x\}$ (outdegree + indegree).
falsification_gate: an $x$ with $\deg x\ne\tau+R$

title: Orientation is not shown to be intrinsic
statement: Whether the orientation (increasing direction) of the SELECT-II digraph can be recovered from the unlabelled graph $G$ alone is open; the integer order is used in the frozen definition.
falsification_gate: an isomorphism-invariant rule recovering orientation (or a proof that none exists)

title: Directed histories are not universal
statement: In the SELECT-II digraph every arrow multiplies by $\ge4$, so the digraph is acyclic and a directed waypoint sequence is strictly increasing. No sequence with a descent (e.g.\ $2,1$) is a waypoint sequence of a directed history. Universality of U3 is a property of the \emph{reversible} graph $G$ (inverse moves), not of SELECT-II's native dynamics.
falsification_gate: a directed path from $m$ to $t<m$

title: Markov no-go vs marks
statement: Frozen S2.13 (continuations depend on the endpoint only) is consistent with U3: memory beyond the endpoint lives entirely in the marks, i.e.\ in declared information.
falsification_gate: a continuation rule using history without marks

title: SELECT-I routes are edges
statement: SELECT-I anchor routes $(k,d)$ with value $kd^2$ correspond to edges $k(d-1)\to kd^2$ (frozen S2.5). SELECT-I's binary continuation/join questions ($J_{\mathrm{join}}$, $J_{\mathrm{ref}}$) concern a \emph{binary} structure; the unary graph $G$ carries none, and U3/U4 claim nothing about it.
status: Proved by S2.5; binary part: not addressed
falsification_gate: a route not equal to an edge

title: FIELD-I integer slice
statement: Frozen F.T1 with $b=1$: occurrences of the integer $a$ are $\{d\ge2:d^2\mid a\}$, of size $R(a)=\operatorname{indeg}(a)$. Rational (non-anchor) outputs, the collective operator $C(x)=x+L^2/G$ and all FIELD dynamics are \emph{not} represented in $G$ (unsupported extension).
falsification_gate: integer fibre size $\ne R(a)$

title: Marks are label recovery, not relational invariants
statement: FIELD-I's leakage criterion (label recovery alone fails the nontrivial-invariant criterion) classifies the U3 decoder as \emph{representation}: it recovers labels from marks. No relational invariant is claimed.
falsification_gate: a relational invariant extracted without marks

title: GIG history counts vs segmentation counts
statement: GIG's $A(t)=\log_2|F_t|$ counts \emph{directed} complete histories into $t$; U3's $M(w)$ counts mark placements on an \emph{undirected} geodesic. They are different quantities; no relation is claimed.
falsification_gate: a proven relation between $A(t)$ and $M$

title: GIG hierarchy vs U3 ledger
statement: The GIG projection hierarchy $T\subset(M,Q)\subset C\subset W$ and the U3 ledger could be related on the class of monotone (forward-only) marked walks; this requires defining directed marked walks first. Not claimed.
falsification_gate: a definition and a theorem

title: Universality half
statement: For every countable alphabet $A$ and injection $e$: faithful marked representation (T1), computable (T2), exact ambiguity $2^{L-1}$ (T3), finite alphabets at cost $\le2$ per transition (T4); dynamics via suspension with return-map conjugacy, Abramov relation, entropy by the pressure equation, period/mixing criteria, and exact embedding-dependence statements (U4.2).
hypotheses: Union of hypotheses of the cited claims.
status: Assembled (new parts: T2, T4, T5, U4.2-T4)
falsification_gate: failure of any cited claim

title: Obstruction half
statement: Finite-memory metric admissibility cannot realise: golden mean, any SFT with $f\ge1$ fixed points on other than $f$ constant letters, memory-1 SFTs with non-real spectrum, full $k$-shifts ($k\ge3$) at radius $1$, any non-SFT; and the directed SELECT-II dynamics cannot represent descents. Whether symmetric memory-1 SFTs are all realisable (Cj1) and whether $G$ is rigid (Cj2) remain open.
falsification_gate: failure of any cited claim

title: Boundary statement
statement: Universal representation (TU) + specified dynamical preservation (U4.2) + explicit information accounting (U4.4) + intrinsic admissibility boundaries (TO): everything beyond finite-memory metric admissibility --- markers, embeddings, route tables, observers, sequence-specific controllers --- is declared additional information.
falsification_gate: a property attributed to the graph that uses a marker not in the ledger
